result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn the switch into a keyboard-operable button with role="switch", aria-checked and a proper accessible name, and both add busy, saved and error feedback to Save. B is the better tidy-up: it gives both controls an explicit focus ring, styles the Save button, sets a readable font and keeps the request exactly as it was. A adds a Content-Type header that changes the request, leaves the Save button unstyled, and gives Save no focus style of its own. A's error message is a little clearer, and neither answer adds an on/off cue beyond color and the thumb's position. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the switch a real button with role="switch", label it correctly, and add busy, saved and error feedback with a working retry. A also styles the Save button, gives the switch and Save matching focus rings, and keeps the exact fetch call. B leaves Save unstyled and adds a Content-Type header the server never asked for, though B does flag that change and adds reduced-motion support and a red error message. A wrongly says the markup is unchanged, but its visual cleanup is more complete.
